original_question: Which gene encodes a protein with six coiled-coil domains, whose mutations cause Seckel syndrome?

final_qi.question: Which gene encodes a protein with six coiled-coil domains, whose mutations cause Seckel syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Mutations in the CEP63 gene, which encodes the centrosomal protein of 63 kDa containing six predicted coiled-coil domains, have been shown to cause Seckel syndrome by disrupting centrosome integrity and impairing ATR-dependent DNA-damage signaling during neurodevelopment.

final_answer.long_answer: The CENPJ gene (centromere protein J, also called CPAP) encodes a centrosomal protein that is composed of six predicted coiled-coil domains. Loss-of-function or missense mutations in CENPJ disrupt centrosome integrity and spindle formation, leading to the microcephaly, dwarfism and other features that define autosomal-recessive Seckel syndrome.
